eventMetadata.context_description: Mexico City's high-elevation subtropical highland climate keeps typical August daytime maxima near 23–24 °C, with the market clustering tightly around 21–23 °C because afternoon convective clouds and showers—common during the peak of the rainy season—frequently cap temperatures by reducing insolation and enhancing evaporative cooling. Current model guidance points to a mix of morning sun followed by building cumulus and scattered thunderstorms, a pattern that historically trims peaks by 1–2 °C relative to clear-sky potential. Minor differences in the timing or coverage of these showers, along with any late adjustments in steering flow or moisture transport from the Pacific, will determine whether the mercury reaches the upper or lower end of the narrow implied-probability band. Official Servicio Meteorológico Nacional and international model updates through the next 24 hours remain the key data points for traders.
